# botyard_bot_member (Resource)

Puts one person on a Botyard bot's member list. When the bot's `access` is `restricted`, only its members can use it; owners also manage its access and members.

**Non-authoritative.** Each resource manages exactly one membership and ignores every other row on the list, so members added in the Botyard app and pending invitations never show up as drift. Declare one resource per person. Several of these resources on the same bot apply safely in parallel: each changes only its own row.

**Existing rows are adopted.** Creating this resource for someone who is already a member takes that row over and sets its `role`; it is not an error. Destroying the resource removes the row, whoever created it.

**Who may change members.** Only a bot owner can change its member list. An API key owns only the bots it created, so manage memberships with the key that created the bot.

**Last owner.** Botyard refuses a change that would leave the bot's member list without an owner. Give someone else `role = "owner"` first, or `terraform state rm` this resource to leave the row outside Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A restricted bot is usable only by its members. Each botyard_bot_member puts
# one person on the list and leaves every other row alone, so members added in
# the Botyard app never show up as drift.
resource "botyard_bot" "assistant" {
  name   = "Assistant"
  access = "restricted"
}

resource "botyard_bot_member" "analyst" {
  bot_slug = botyard_bot.assistant.slug
  user_id  = "5f0c2a4e-9b1d-4e7a-8c3f-2d6b1a9e0f47"
}

# A co-owner can change the bot's access mode and member list in the app.
resource "botyard_bot_member" "lead" {
  bot_slug = botyard_bot.assistant.slug
  user_id  = "9a3e7c1b-2d4f-4b6a-8e0c-7f1d2a3b4c5d"
  role     = "owner"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bot_slug` (String) Slug of the bot, e.g. `botyard_bot.x.slug`. Changing it forces replacement.
- `user_id` (String) ID of the user. They must be a member of the organization. Changing it forces replacement.

### Optional

- `role` (String) `member` (uses the bot) or `owner` (also manages its access and members). Defaults to `member`. Updated in place.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the membership was created (RFC 3339). For an adopted row this is when it was first created, not when Terraform took it over.
- `email` (String) The member's email address.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier: `{bot_slug}/{user_id}`.
- `name` (String) The member's display name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Memberships are imported by `{bot_slug}/{user_id}`.
terraform import botyard_bot_member.analyst assistant/5f0c2a4e-9b1d-4e7a-8c3f-2d6b1a9e0f47
```
